name: miraDry
lead: miraDry is a non-invasive microwave device made by Miramar Labs that heats tissue in the armpit to destroy sweat glands. It has been cleared by the US FDA and Health Canada for axillary hyperhidrosis and is also used for underarm odor [1][2].

Treatment typically involves local anesthetic injection into the armpit followed by application of the microwave emitter to the skin [3]. A 2022 review of microwave technology in dermatology covers its use for axillary hyperhidrosis and osmidrosis among other conditions [1].
Several clinical studies and a patient survey have been published, and case reports document rare serious complications including brachial plexus nerve injury and a fatal infection [3][4][6][7].

paras: The system delivers microwave energy through the skin to heat the layer where sweat glands sit. Because glands are destroyed rather than temporarily blocked, the aim is a longer-lasting effect than topical products or botulinum toxin. A registered trial studied axillary hair loss after treatment [8].

Registered trials include a 2010 study in 31 people with hyperhidrosis [9], a 2014 study of focal axillary hyperhidrosis that was terminated [10], a 2020 patient satisfaction and safety study in 100 people [11], and a 2021 trial comparing the longevity of microwave thermolysis with botulinum toxin in 30 people [12]. A 2012 trial compared a 1440 nm laser with botulinum toxin or miraDry [13]. A study of microwave ablation in mild axillary hidradenitis suppurativa was terminated with 9 participants [14].

Published reports include a 2023 analysis of single-session high-energy microwave therapy for hyperhidrosis and osmidrosis that discussed pretreatment factors that may lower complication risk [4], a 2024 retrospective comparison of microwave therapy and suction-curettage [5], a 2024 patient satisfaction survey [6], and 2025 and 2026 studies including a three-year follow-up [7][15]. Their detailed findings are not summarised here.

Wikipedia notes rare but serious risks including upper-limb paralysis and brachial plexus injury [16]. Case reports describe brachial plexus injury after treatment in a thin 49-year-old woman [3] and a thin 19-year-old man, managed conservatively [17]. A 2022 case report describes necrotizing fasciitis with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome with a fatal outcome after treatment [18], and another case report describes complications following microwave treatment [19].
Authors have described a 'danger zone' for nerve injury and have discussed pretreatment assessment to reduce risk [4].

timeline.event: Early registered clinical evaluations of the miraDry system in hyperhidrosis begin [9].
Case report of bilateral brachial plexus injury published [3].
Fatal necrotizing fasciitis case report published [18].

card.summary: A microwave device that destroys underarm sweat glands in a clinic; studied in several trials, with rare but serious nerve-injury and infection case reports.
card.note: Case reports document brachial plexus injury and one fatal infection.

quick.overview:
miraDry is an FDA-cleared microwave device used in clinics to destroy underarm sweat glands, mainly for heavy sweating and sometimes odor. Treatment is done under local anesthetic.

Several registered trials, patient surveys and a three-year follow-up have been published, alongside case reports of complications.
quick.mechanism: Microwave energy heats the tissue layer containing sweat glands, destroying them so they stop producing sweat.
quick.risks: Case reports describe brachial plexus (nerve) injury, and one fatal necrotizing fasciitis case. Authors have discussed a nerve-injury 'danger zone' and pretreatment assessment.
